text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
All newspapers lead with handover of Hong Kong to China at midnight on Monday.
-- The government will continue to monitor its spending to avoid wastage and excessive expenditure, acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said.

-- All development projects which involve environmentally sensitive areas in Selangor must be referred to the Department of Environment before approval is given, irrespective of whether they are subject to the Environmental Impact Assessment.
-- Banks have stopped printing the account numbers on automated teller machine transaction slips in a move to prevent cloning of ATM cards, Association of Banks Malaysia chairman Amirsham Aziz said.

-- Malayan United Industries Bhd (MUI) whose top investment in Hong Kong is its 25.8 percent stake in newspaper South China Morning Post Ltd, believes that post-handover Hong Kong will be BUSINESS TIMES

-- Owing to the restrained trading conditions on the local bourse in the past few months, the number of companies with a market capitalisation of a billion ringgit or more fell to 163 as of Monday, from a record 166 at end-1996.

-- Malaysia Mining Corp (MMC) and Finnish utility Imatran Voima Oy may be part of the Tenaga Nasional Bhd-led consortium to be tasked with privatising the Sabah Electricity Board. MMC "could possibly be" one of the companies, Minister of Energy, Telecommunications and Posts Leo Moggie said last week.
